items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Wonderful wife, Evelyn, grew up together

ctx.x: He saw me one summer day after Reverend Turner made that fiddle, he was coming through the alley and I'm on the back porch playing with it and he said, "Let me play it." I said, "You think you can play it?" He said, "Yeah." He grabbed it and naturally he didn't know nothing about it. He was a beautiful person. So I took it from him. He said, "One of these days, I'm going to get my own fiddle." Sure enough, he

did. Brilliant dude. He loves Jimmy Blanton (PHONETIC). To me, the young man can play almost every solo Jimmy has played. He's a father of about seven, eight children, now a grandfather like myself. But he's not playing regular. It's kind of hard for him. But he's doing beautiful, though. Wonderful wife, Evelyn, grew up together, and they stuck together, which is what it's all about.

Well, anyway, I decided to come back to New York. That was around August, around July. I left Chicago just before the riot started out there, and I got to New York, where they had another riot up there in Harlem. That's when Lindsay walked the streets, you know, (unintelligible) doing all that.
